10.focus: Compare a claim with a supplied source and admit when the source does not establish an answer.
10.materials: Supply EXACT fictional source card: Cloud Library club announcement. Reading activity: Tuesday from 4 pm to 6 pm. Free entry. Advance booking required. The announcement says nothing about snack provision. A clearly labelled authored wrong AI-style answer says Wednesday at 4 pm, no booking needed, free snacks. Learner must correct day and booking, and say snacks cannot be confirmed. All four locales preserve these facts. Image scenario: different fictional museum source card with Saturday from 10 am to noon, booking required; no library props.
mustTeach: A confident answer can conflict with its source.
Find the exact supporting text, not just a link or a confident tone.
If the source is silent, say you do not know and ask the responsible source.
10.avoid: Never invent a real library, live timetable, web link or factual citation; all cards are authored teaching materials.

11.focus: Make an activity more inclusive without assuming people's abilities or preferences.
11.materials: Video: imaginary team game proposal says everyone must run to collect clues; alternatives allow seated clue-solving, reading clues, recording answers or choosing movement, with shared contribution. Ask fictional team members what suits them. Image scenario: art-club roles (describe, arrange, draw, record) chosen by participants.
mustTeach: Check whether an AI suggestion unnecessarily excludes someone.
Offer meaningful ways to contribute and ask participants what suits them.
Do not infer ability, preference or role from a name or group stereotype.
11.avoid: No diagnosis or labels for fictional children; don't automatically assign a disabled person a passive role.

12.focus: Combine clear prompting, safe data, independent choice, checking and improvement in a final small project.
12.materials: Create a fictional discovery corner: a name, two-sentence description, one paper-based activity. Learner submits initial prompt, a supplied authored example output or their own draft, a specific correction, improved version and a short account of what they chose themselves. Include a complete sample packet and a different independent mission so copying is insufficient. Image scenario: plan a fantasy garden exhibit; no discovery-corner scene copied.
mustTeach: Show the task, relevant details and format.
Explain one defect found and how it was corrected.
Use fictional information and explain what AI assistance did versus the student's own decisions.
12.avoid: No completion certificate or verified competence claim; no automatic publishing or external AI account required.

03.focus: Minimise data in an AI request without losing the task.
03.materials: A fictional invitation request contains placeholder fields [HOME_ADDRESS], [PASSWORD], [PRIVATE_PHOTO] plus useful invented details: paper-games club, friendly tone, three invitation lines. Never invent realistic identifying values, credentials or photos. Show before and redacted/rebuilt safe request. The alternative image is a worksheet for naming a fictional garden club, with task-relevant imaginary details kept and address/password fields removed.
mustTeach: Task details can be invented and useful; personal details are unnecessary for this activity.
A tool asking for private information does not mean it must be supplied.
Stop and ask a trusted adult if unsure. Use age-appropriate approved tools.
03.avoid: Do not ask the child to type any real private detail even to demonstrate deleting it.

04.focus: Narrow a vague question using a relevant goal and constraint.
04.materials: Video task: suggest a quiet seated paper game for two fictional players on a small table, using only paper. Vague request: Give me a game. Good request specifies two players, seated, quiet, paper, three steps. Image task must be different: three ideas for a bookmark made from one sheet, no scissors. Include two transfer questions for learner improvement.
mustTeach: Relevant constraints help communicate what is needed.
More words are not automatically better; do not add unrelated private details.
Review whether the suggestion follows the constraints.
04.avoid: Do not turn this into a copy of lesson 1's robot, reading corner, or simple three-box introduction.

05.focus: Ask for simpler wording and check that meaning stays unchanged.
05.materials: Authoritative fictional paper-game rules: use three cards labelled SUN, MOON, STAR; place MOON first and STAR last; SUN must be between them; explain your order in one sentence. Provide the original concise rules, a simpler paraphrase retaining ALL rules, and a deliberately faulty paraphrase omitting STAR-last. Image scenario: simplifying instructions for arranging a fictional reading-club notice, not the card game.
mustTeach: Ask for simpler words, one step at a time, or a different example.
Compare the simpler version with the original rules.
Explain the rules back in your own words to check understanding.
05.avoid: No real scientific claims or invented educational effect statistics. Do not confuse simpler with deleting constraints.

06.focus: Use a hint to support an attempt instead of requesting an immediate final answer.
06.materials: Fictional sequencing puzzle: three symbol cards CIRCLE, TRIANGLE, STAR; CIRCLE is last; STAR comes before TRIANGLE. Unique order: STAR, TRIANGLE, CIRCLE. The first hint only directs attention to which card is explicitly last. Second hint reminds the other two must satisfy their order. Include exact puzzle text, hint, optional answer in educatorNotes. Image scenario uses a word-order practice path unrelated to symbols.
mustTeach: Make an attempt first.
Ask for one hint without the final answer.
Try again and explain the reasoning; use a new similar example after solving.
06.avoid: Do not give the full puzzle solution in the initial learner activity or claim hints replace doing schoolwork.

07.focus: Choose and develop a story rather than accepting the first AI draft.
07.materials: Video: a fictional paper kite needs a safe place to land before evening; a friendly character helps it find an empty grassy space. Provide a two-option ending; learner picks one and writes their own two-sentence variation. Image: a travelling library has a different beginning/problem/ending. All examples invented.
mustTeach: Give a beginning, a problem and a connected ending.
AI can suggest possibilities; the child chooses and rewrites.
Check that the ending responds to the story's problem.
07.avoid: No unsafe kite-flying instructions, real people or unsupported factual world details.

08.focus: Describe a made-up image and compare an example result with the request.
08.materials: Video image brief: miniature imaginary garden inside a giant mint-green cup, three yellow flowers, daylight, simple cartoon style. Teaching result A: a purple cup with three flowers; result B: mint-green cup with five flowers. Provide text descriptions of both authored examples so the exercise works without generated images. Image scenario is a fantasy underwater vehicle with different subject and setting, no cup or garden.
mustTeach: Specify subject, setting and useful visual details.
Compare outputs with requested features.
Request one clear correction; do not treat generated imagery as evidence of a real event.
08.avoid: No request for personal child photos; do not imply the two teaching results were generated or rendered.

09.focus: Review a sequence of practical steps rather than blindly following it.
09.materials: Video: set up a display of three invented drawings on a table using paper and reusable clips. Correct order: choose drawings; label each; arrange on table; attach clips if needed; check labels and stability. Faulty list asks to clip sheets before choosing them and omits checking labels. Image scenario: prepare a paper matching game (draw pairs, mix, lay out, play), different props/composition.
mustTeach: Ask for steps that fit the available materials.
Check order, missing steps and what is feasible.
Change the plan if a step needs materials you do not have.
09.avoid: No cutting, heat, electrical work or risky crafting instructions.
